rationale: Allocation profiling (heaptrack + custom GlobalAlloc counters; DHAT attempted but abandoned — Valgrind serializes threads, hiding Rayon contention) + Plonky3/SP1/Jolt alloc survey. 13M allocs, 16.7GB total per run. Top sites: #1 bit_reverse_chunks 3.2GB (GKR), #2 WhirConfig::round 312MB, #3 fold_multilinear_at_bit 156MB, #4-19 Rayon par_collect ~1.4GB, #20 MerkleTree::from_first_layer 62MB. Patterns: Plonky3 for_each_init, Jolt unsafe_allocate_zero_vec + spare_capacity_mut, SP1 WorkerQueue pooling.

Fused unpack_extension+bit_reverse_chunks into single-pass to eliminate ~1.6GB intermediate Vec. Correct but no measurable speedup: only 2 large allocs eliminated, bench uses mimalloc which handles large allocs efficiently. Wrong target — need to focus on the ~4M small par_collect allocs not the few large ones.

Changed eval_fn from Vec<T> to &[T] in 4 sumcheck functions, pre-allocated point_buf/diff_buf per parallel work item. Eliminates per-k-iteration .collect() in split_eq variants (from packed_hi*(degree+1) allocs to 2 per item). Glibc bench: -0.62%, p=0.01. Real but below 1.0% gate. Small n_cols (2-40 elements) means each eliminated alloc was cheap. Need deeper approach: for_each_init to eliminate ALL per-call allocs, or target other hotspots.

Replaced into_par_iter().chunks() with par_chunks_exact() in compute_eval_eq_packed and compute_eval_eq_base_packed. Rayon chunks() creates a Vec per chunk — 9.09M allocs (70% of total) from WHIR equality updates calling this per STIR query. Fix: use slice-based par_chunks_exact (zero-alloc). Allocs: 12.94M→3.64M (-71.8%). Glibc bench: -2.12%, p=0.00. Gate passed.

Override vertically_packed_row_rtl on DenseMatrix (zero-alloc direct indexing) and FlatMatrixView (1 alloc via inner wrapping_row_slices instead of 17). Merkle build allocs: 1.62M→14K (-99.1%). Glibc bench: -0.47%, p=0.00. Real but below 1.0% gate — each eliminated alloc was tiny (~128B wrapping_row_slices Vecs).

In-place bit_reverse_chunks to eliminate output Vec allocation in unpack_and_unreverse_active. Saves 20 large (>1MB) allocs. Glibc bench: -0.22%, p=0.02. Negligible — large alloc/dealloc is fast in glibc.

Pre-allocate trace column Vecs in parallel batch segments with capacity derived from first iteration. Eliminates ~210K reallocation cascade allocs across 1399 parallel segments × ~170 columns. Allocs: 3.64M→3.44M (-5.7%). Glibc bench: -3.25%, p=0.00. Big win from reduced allocator contention in Rayon threads.

Override vertically_packed_row_rtl on DenseMatrix (zero-alloc direct indexing with precomputed row offsets) and FlatMatrixView (1 alloc via inner wrapping_row_slices, not 17). Phase 14 allocs: 1.62M->14.4K (-99.1%). Total allocs: 3.44M->1.77M (-48.5%). Glibc bench: -1.90%, p=0.00. Precomputed row offsets avoid modulo in inner loop.

files_changed: Replaced 2 get_slice() calls (Vec alloc via collect) with 16 individual get() calls into stack array. Regression +1.13%, p=0.00. Per-element get() through trait dispatch slower than batch get_slice() despite eliminating 2 small Vec allocs.
Fused read+trace loop eliminating 4 of 5 Vec allocs in exec_multi_row. Regression +0.71%, p=0.00. Extra trace column indexing for deferred VRES/COMP fill added overhead exceeding alloc savings.
FlatMatrixView zero-alloc vertically_packed_row_rtl via flat_buffer + precomputed row offsets. Phase 14: 14K allocs eliminated. Noise (+0.31%, p=0.00). 14K alloc reduction too small to matter.

Thread-local Vec pool for exec_multi_row: 5 Vecs recycled per call via TLS. Phase 1 allocs: 1.48M->1.32M (-10.7%). Glibc bench: +0.08%, p=0.41. TLS lookup overhead equals alloc savings; glibc thread-local tcache already handles small Vecs efficiently.

Added get_slice_into() buffer-based API to MemoryAccess trait; poseidon_16 writes to stack array instead of allocating Vec. Phase 1 allocs: 1.48M->434K (-70.6%). Total: 1.77M->724K (-59.0%). 372 poseidon calls/seg × 2 get_slice = 744 elim allocs/seg. Glibc: +0.05%, p=0.63. Each Vec was 32B (8×F) — tcache near-zero cost.

Parallelized memory_acc/bytecode_acc building with AtomicU32 + Rayon par_chunks. Replaces sequential F::ONE += with atomic fetch_add(1, Relaxed), converts to F at end. Glibc bench: +0.31%, p=0.00. Regression — lock xadd overhead (~20-30ns) exceeds sequential load+add+store (~15ns) for this memory-bound random-access pattern. 1M entry array fits L3; parallelism adds contention without bandwidth benefit.

rationale: Direct indexing in compute_raw_poly_impl: replaced clear+push loop with pre-sized arrays for point/diff buffers. Eliminates Vec::clear()+push() overhead in inner sumcheck loop. Glibc bench: +0.4615

rationale: Override WHIR FlatMatrixView::vertically_packed_row_rtl to use inner DenseMatrix row slices directly (zero alloc vs 16 Vecs per call). Alloc counter: 12,940K→11,334K (-1,606K allocs, -12.4%), 468MB less total. Wall-clock: 5136ms vs 5146ms (+0.2%) — ZERO effect. glibc tcache absorbs all small alloc overhead (~10ns each = ~16ms total for 1.6M allocs = 0.3% of runtime). Allocation-reduction surface conclusively exhausted.

Batched STIR equality updates with L2-tiled output traversal. Instead of 274 sequential full sweeps of ~84MB weight buffer, split output into 2^14-element tiles (320KB, fits L2) and process all 274 queries per tile. Eq poly's multiplicative structure allows O(n-k) prefix scalar per tile. DRAM traffic: ~67GB→~168MB. Two runs: -17.4%, -16.2%, both p=0.00. Cache-traffic optimization, not allocation reduction.
